title: An NTT/INTT Accelerator with Ultra-High Throughput and Area Efficiency for FHE
problem: Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) of large degree in Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is the primary source of computational and time overhead. Memory bandwidth limitations create a critical bottleneck constraining NTT/INTT throughput.
motivation: Fully Homomorphic Encryption requires efficient NTT/INTT acceleration to become practically deployable; improving throughput and area efficiency is essential for real-world FHE systems.
method: The accelerator uses a conflict-free memory mapping algorithm—a technique that stores data so different computational steps can access what they need simultaneously without waiting. This eliminates the memory bandwidth constraint that normally limits NTT/INTT performance. The design pairs this with a hardware/software pipeline that operates continuously without pausing, achieving 48,543+ operations per second on large transforms where N=2^16 (65,536 data points).
key_novelty: The core idea is conflict-free memory mapping—storing data so different computational operations don't interfere when accessing it—which breaks the memory bandwidth bottleneck and enables nonstop NTT/INTT pipeline execution.
contributions: Scalable conflict-free memory mapping algorithm for NTT that eliminates memory conflicts and frees on-chip resources
Flexible no-stall hardware/software pipeline architecture for high-throughput NTT/INTT computation
Achieves 48,543+ operations/second for N=2^16 with improved area efficiency
Demonstrates 4x speedup over prior FPGA-based scheme and 10x over GPU-based scheme (HPCA'23)
limitations: Scalability to other transform sizes, practical deployment constraints, and power consumption characteristics not discussed.
